_comment: Seed for the chat-model context table. Keys are FULL model ids, never family wildcards: glm-5.2 has a 1M window while glm-5.1 has 200K, so a 'glm-5*' pattern would misreport by 5x. Every row cites the official vendor page it was read from; a row without a citation is a test failure, not a data choice (tests/test_model_router_context_table.py). TWO consumers read these rows. (1) vco_lib.vscode_settings.decorate_1m appends Claude Code's own '[1m]' context hint to a slot/default value naming a 1M model — the client assumes 200K for a plain id like claude-fable-5-1 (field symptom: '0% context remaining' right after compaction), and it reads the 'window_1m' flag. (2) The gateway's /v1/models DOES read these rows, as of v0.2.95: model_router.catalog.resolve_window treats a cited row here as the highest authority below a tombstone, and the 'context_window' it yields decides both the row's description and whether the catalog publishes an '[1m]' companion. (An earlier version of this note said the gateway did not read them and that first-party ids were published verbatim; both were true then and neither is now.) Because the two consumers read DIFFERENT fields, keep 'window_1m' and 'context_window' in agreement — the gateway logs a warning when a row contradicts itself. Window/output figures are the vendor's own decimal-K figures, not powers of two. This file is the FALLBACK: the launcher exports a user-editable table to <vct_root>/model-gateway/chat_model_context.json, and that export wins per ROW when present. Window figures must come from the VENDOR'S PER-MODEL SPEC TABLE: an integration page (e.g. QwenCloud's Claude Code page) quotes the CLIENT's default window (200K) and describes raising it, which is not a per-model window — every qwen-vendor row here read 200000 in v0.2.97 for exactly that reason, understating a real 1M by 5x.

qwen.source_note: v0.2.100 (F-W1-19): the QwenCloud per-model table lists glm-5.2 at '198k' on its endpoint (read 2026-09-29), so the copy that route serves must not be advertised as '[1m]' — the z.ai figure above is the model's window on z.ai's endpoint, not on this one. '198k' is read as 198,000 (the decimal reading, which never overstates; the vendor multiplies some figures by 1024). max_output 0 = not stated in the cited line: no output figure is published for this route rather than borrowing z.ai's.

glm-4.5-air.source_note: This model has no page of its own (https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-4.5-air returns 404); its specification sits on the GLM-4.5 card, which is what the cited URL is. Third-party listings of a 1M variant of this model are NOT official and are deliberately not reflected here.

qwen3.8-max.source_note: Window and output are the vendor's PER-MODEL figures on the cited page. The 200000 this row carried until v0.2.98 came from the Claude Code integration page's sentence about the CLIENT's default window, which is not a per-model spec; that citation is gone. The vendor writes output as '128k'/'64k' without expanding it — its DeepSeek '384k' expands to 393,216 (= 384*1024) — so the decimal readings are the non-overstating choice. The same vendor's Claude Code config for this endpoint sets CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=983616 (1,000,000 - 16,384) with no stated rationale, but VCO writes no such knob (docs/CONFIGURATION.md, 'Panel mode'), so the 1M here is the documented model window. (Qwen3.8 table.)

qwen3.8-flash.source_note: See qwen3.8-max; same page, Qwen3.8 table.

qwen3.7-max.source_note: See qwen3.8-max; same page, Qwen3.7 table.

qwen3.7-plus.source_note: See qwen3.8-max; same page, Qwen3.7 table. The integration page's [1m] example used this id, but that was a mechanism example, not a capability claim — the window here is the vendor's own per-model table.

qwen3.6-flash.source_note: See qwen3.8-max; same page, Qwen3.6 table.

deepseek-v4-pro.source_note: See qwen3.8-max (same page). Also cited: the deepseek page, whose 'Parameter defaults' give max_tokens 393,216 — a budget SHARED between output and thinking, so max_output here is that shared ceiling, not an output-only one. 384k expands to 393,216 because the vendor multiplies by 1024.

Also cited: the deepseek page, whose 'Parameter defaults' give max_tokens 393,216 — a budget SHARED between output and thinking, so max_output here is that shared ceiling, not an output-only one. 384k expands to 393,216 because the vendor multiplies by 1024. Present on the subscription's live compatible-mode model list (probe 2026-09-22).

deepseek-v4.1-flash.source_note: See qwen3.8-max (same page). Also cited: the deepseek page, whose 'Parameter defaults' give max_tokens 393,216 — a budget SHARED between output and thinking, so max_output here is that shared ceiling, not an output-only one. 384k expands to 393,216 because the vendor multiplies by 1024. Present on the subscription's live compatible-model list (probe 2026-09-22), which the previously cited integration page predates.

claude-fable-5-1.source_note: First-party row, read by TWO consumers: vco_lib.vscode_settings.decorate_1m (reads window_1m, so a slot/default naming this model carries the client's own [1m] hint) and the gateway catalog (reads context_window; the plain id is published verbatim AND an '[1m]' companion row is published beside it). An earlier version of this note said the gateway did not advertise these rows; that stopped being true in v0.2.95.
